claims.text: An identity is a low-level Platform construct: one or more public keys recorded on the platform chain plus a credit balance, used to own data and sign state transitions, and kept separate from DPNS usernames.
A Core (layer-1) wallet address is a legacy Base58Check address used on the money layer to hold and move Dash, and is distinct from Platform's independent bech32m address system (DIP-18).

A Platform address is a bech32m-encoded layer-2 address (dash1.../tdash1...) that holds credits directly and is used for address-based operations such as funding identity creation, independent of any identity.

An identity balances the Core address / Platform address contrast: it is not an address at all, but a key set plus a credit balance; its 32-byte id is produced from a double SHA-256 of the funding outpoint rather than from a public key hash.

Creating an identity locks Dash on Core in an asset lock transaction; that lock is proven in an identity create state transition, and the locked value (minus fees) becomes the identity's initial credit balance.
An identity's credit balance can be topped up by locking more Dash; anyone may top up any identity, which lets developers subsidize their users' usage.
Each identity holds one or more public keys; every key carries a purpose (authentication, encryption, decryption, transfer) describing what it may be used for.
Every key also carries a security level (master, critical, high, medium) describing how carefully it should be stored; the master key is required and can only be used to update the identity.
Every identity must have exactly one master-level authentication key used for updating the identity; additional authentication and transfer keys are strongly recommended.
Wallets conventionally derive five standard identity keys (DIP-9): master, high authentication, critical authentication, transfer, and encryption (medium).

Identity keys are derived from the wallet mnemonic via DIP-13 feature path m/9'/coin'/5'/0'/0'/{identityIndex}'/{keyIndex}', while addresses use BIP44 — so one wallet seed derives both addresses and identity keys.
Credits are the layer-2 unit of account for fees; the conversion is 1 duff = 1,000 credits (CREDITS_PER_DUFF), so 1 Dash = 100,000,000 duffs = 100,000,000,000 credits.

Platform fees are divided into storage fees (cost of keeping data across the network) and processing fees (cost of validating state transitions); they are paid by deducting credits from the identity's balance.
For everyday use processing fees are minuscule compared to storage fees, but they become prohibitively expensive in attack conditions.
Credits can be converted back to Dash via an identity credit withdrawal state transition, subject to a daily network-wide limit.

conflicts.resolution: Keep module 3 conceptual: state only 1 duff = 1,000 credits and the storage-vs-processing split; quote no per-byte or per-key fee constants, which belong to later hands-on lessons.

conflicts.topic: mustCover names two objects but the acceptance test names four
conflicts.resolution: Distinguish Core wallet/address, Platform address, and Platform identity in prose and a comparison table, naming each without the DIP-18 derivation mechanics reserved for module 9.

conflicts.topic: How deep identity keys should go relative to module 10
conflicts.resolution: Name the purposes (authentication, encryption, decryption, transfer) and security levels (master/critical/high/medium) and the mandatory master-level authentication key, without the full purpose/security-level allowlist or signing-behavior details.
